To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single session of power exercise can cause beneficial changes on the hemodynamic profile of older women.
an acute session power and resistance exercise may be beneficial to induce changes on hemodynamic measurements and nitric oxide in older women.
an acute session (one session) of resistance exercise can be an effective method to induce beneficial changes on hemodynamics and NO levels in elderly women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of physical exercise on hemodynamic parameters, and NO bioavailability in older women.
the effects of power and resistive exercises in older women.
the acute effects of RT and PT on the hemodynamic measurements of systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), heart rate (HR), and double product (DP) of older women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
power training and resistance training can induce similar effects in older women.
power exercise can be more efficient than RT to induce post-exercise hypolipidemia in older adults.
power exercise is more efficient to decrease systolic blood pressure and increase NO bioavailability in older women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a single session of power exercise can be an effective tool to cause beneficial changes in the hemodynamic parameters in the short-term, and resistance exercise is effective to improve the NO bioavailability in the short-term.
the acute effects of PT and RT are similar in older women.
power training is as effective as resistance training in improving hemodynamic parameters and bioavailability of NO in older women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acute effects of PT and RT are not similar, and the effects of PT on hemodynamic and NO measurements are more evident.
power and resistance exercise are safe and effective in improving cardiovascular health of older women.
power and resistance exercise are equally effective to induce beneficial changes in hemodynamic parameters and salivary NO levels in older adults.
